Someone is about to build a three-layer analytical platform in a fresh repo:
- DAS: dlt ingests a public OData API, lands parquet, unpacked into DuckDB as views. Schemas das__raw, das__staged.
- DAB: daana-cli (a Go binary) builds a focal/ensemble model. Schemas dab, dab__stage, dab__meta.

import json, os, sys, hashlib
from datetime import datetime, timezone
import requests
import dlt

BASE = "https://demodata.grapecity.com/northwind/odata/v1/Orders"
LAKE = os.path.abspath("./_lake")

def fetch(top=60, skip=0):
    url = f"{BASE}?$count=true&$top={top}&$skip={skip}"
    r = requests.get(url, timeout=60)
    r.raise_for_status()
    body = r.json()
    return url, body

def rows(top=60):
    url, body = fetch(top)
    ts = datetime.now(timezone.utc).isoformat()
    for i, rec in enumerate(body["value"]):
        yield url, ts, i, body.get("@odata.count"), rec

# ---- A: pre-serialised JSON string, plain text column ----
@dlt.resource(name="orders_a_jsonstr", write_disposition="append")
def orders_a():
    for url, ts, i, cnt, rec in rows():
        payload = json.dumps(rec, separators=(",", ":"), sort_keys=True)
        yield {
            "payload": payload,
            "_src_system": "northwind_odata",
            "_src_entity": "Orders",
            "_src_url": url,
            "_extracted_at": ts,
            "_page_index": i,
            "_src_total_count": cnt,
            "_payload_hash": hashlib.sha256(payload.encode()).hexdigest(),
        }

# ---- B: real dict, column hint data_type="json" ----
@dlt.resource(name="orders_b_jsonhint", write_disposition="append",
              columns={"payload": {"data_type": "json"}})
def orders_b():
    for url, ts, i, cnt, rec in rows():
        yield {
            "payload": rec,
            "_src_url": url,
            "_extracted_at": ts,
            "_page_index": i,
        }

# ---- C: max_table_nesting=0, record spread at top level ----
@dlt.resource(name="orders_c_nest0", write_disposition="append", max_table_nesting=0)
def orders_c():
    for url, ts, i, cnt, rec in rows():
        d = dict(rec)
        d["_src_url"] = url
        yield d

p = dlt.pipeline(
    pipeline_name="das_raw",
    destination=dlt.destinations.filesystem(bucket_url=LAKE),
    dataset_name="das__raw",
)
info = p.run([orders_a(), orders_b(), orders_c()], loader_file_format="parquet")
print(info)
print("=" * 30, "SCHEMA", "=" * 30)
sch = p.default_schema
for tname in ("orders_a_jsonstr", "orders_b_jsonhint", "orders_c_nest0"):
    t = sch.tables.get(tname)
    print(f"--- {tname} ---")
    if t is None:
        print("  MISSING")
        continue
    for cn, c in t["columns"].items():
        print(f"  {cn:24s} {c.get('data_type')}")
print("ALL TABLES IN SCHEMA:", sorted(sch.tables.keys()))

"""DAS forgiving ingestion: one JSON column per source record, append-only parquet."""
import os, uuid, hashlib, json
from datetime import datetime, timezone
import requests, dlt

BASE = "https://demodata.grapecity.com/northwind/odata/v1/Orders"
LAKE = os.path.abspath("./_lake3")
PAGE = 60

@dlt.resource(
    name="orders",
    write_disposition="append",
    columns={"payload": {"data_type": "json"}},   # <-- the whole trick
)
def odata_orders(page_size: int = PAGE, max_pages: int = 2):
    run_id = str(uuid.uuid4())
    for page in range(max_pages):
        url = f"{BASE}?$count=true&$top={page_size}&$skip={page * page_size}"
        resp = requests.get(url, timeout=60)
        resp.raise_for_status()
        fetched_at = datetime.now(timezone.utc)
        body = resp.json()
        for i, rec in enumerate(body["value"]):
            canon = json.dumps(rec, separators=(",", ":"), sort_keys=True)
            yield {
                "payload":            rec,                      # stays ONE json column
                "das_source_system":  "northwind_odata",
                "das_source_entity":  "Orders",
                "das_request_url":    url,
                "das_http_status":    resp.status_code,
                "das_extracted_at":   fetched_at,
                "das_run_id":         run_id,
                "das_page_number":    page,
                "das_page_offset":    i,
                "das_record_hash":    hashlib.sha256(canon.encode()).hexdigest(),
                "das_source_count":   body.get("@odata.count"),
            }

pipeline = dlt.pipeline(
    pipeline_name="das_ingest",
    destination=dlt.destinations.filesystem(
        bucket_url=LAKE,
        enable_dataset_name_normalization=False,   # keeps the literal 'das__raw'
    ),
    dataset_name="das__raw",
)
info = pipeline.run(odata_orders(), loader_file_format="parquet")
print(info)
print("COLUMNS:", {k: v.get("data_type") for k, v in pipeline.default_schema.tables["orders"]["columns"].items()})
print("TABLES:", sorted(pipeline.default_schema.tables.keys()))

CREATE SCHEMA IF NOT EXISTS das__staged;

  CAST(payload ->> '$.EmployeeId'   AS INTEGER)        AS employee_id,

  das_extracted_at, das_run_id, das_page_number, das_page_offset,
  das_record_hash, das_source_count, das_source_file
FROM das__raw.orders;

    import os, uuid, hashlib, json
    from datetime import datetime, timezone
    import requests, dlt

    LAKE = os.path.abspath("./_lake3")

        name="orders",
        write_disposition="append",
        columns={"payload": {"data_type": "json"}},   # <-- the whole trick
    )
    def odata_orders(page_size: int = PAGE, max_pages: int = 2):
        run_id = str(uuid.uuid4())
        for page in range(max_pages):
            url = f"{BASE}?$count=true&$top={page_size}&$skip={page * page_size}"
            resp = requests.get(url, timeout=60)
            resp.raise_for_status()
            fetched_at = datetime.now(timezone.utc)
            body = resp.json()
            for i, rec in enumerate(body["value"]):
                canon = json.dumps(rec, separators=(",", ":"), sort_keys=True)
                yield {
                    "payload":            rec,                      # stays ONE json column
                    "das_source_system":  "northwind_odata",
                    "das_source_entity":  "Orders",
                    "das_request_url":    url,
                    "das_http_status":    resp.status_code,
                    "das_extracted_at":   fetched_at,
                    "das_run_id":         run_id,
                    "das_page_number":    page,
                    "das_page_offset":    i,
                    "das_record_hash":    hashlib.sha256(canon.encode()).hexdigest(),
                    "das_source_count":   body.get("@odata.count"),
                }

    pipeline = dlt.pipeline(
        pipeline_name="das_ingest",
        destination=dlt.destinations.filesystem(
            bucket_url=LAKE,
            enable_dataset_name_normalization=False,   # keeps the literal 'das__raw'
            # optional: layout="{table_name}/load_date={YYYY}-{MM}-{DD}/{load_id}.{file_id}.{ext}",
        ),
        dataset_name="das__raw",

gotchas: dataset_name='das__raw' is SILENTLY renamed to 'das_raw' (dlt collapses the double underscore). Only a WARNING log line tells you. Fix: dlt.destinations.filesystem(bucket_url=..., enable_dataset_name_normalization=False). If DAS/DAB/DAR all use double-underscore schema names, every dlt destination in the project needs this flag.

DuckDB read_parquet over a glob defaults to the FIRST file's schema and silently drops columns present only in later files — no error, no warning, just missing data. In an append-only lake where you may add a provenance column, always pass union_by_name => true.

max_table_nesting=0 is NOT the answer to 'do not normalise'. It only stops child tables; top-level keys still become snake_cased typed columns. Only the payload+data_type='json' hint (or pre-serialising with json.dumps) gives one column.

dlt's `json` data_type is NOT a parquet JSON logical type. parquet_schema() shows BYTE_ARRAY / UTF8 / StringType() — byte-identical to a text column. Anything downstream reading the parquet sees a VARCHAR, so the strict layer must cast, always.

_dlt_id is regenerated per load. The same source record has a different _dlt_id in every run (10248 was b6aVmzfAxRVPDA then z8O+0F4oaJbS5A). Never use it as a business or record key — add your own content hash.

_dlt_loads, _dlt_pipeline_state and _dlt_version are written as .jsonl even when loader_file_format='parquet'. To get a load's completion timestamp you must read_json_auto() the JSONL, not read_parquet(). Better: put das_extracted_at on every row so das__staged never needs that join.

dlt inferred freight as DOUBLE when it normalised the record (approach C). Money silently becomes floating point. The strict layer casting to DECIMAL(18,4) out of the JSON string is the fix — another reason not to let dlt infer.

Schema evolution is real and late: ship_region only appeared as a column AFTER the first records that had it null, and it landed at the END of the column list. Column ORDER in the parquet is not stable across loads — never rely on positional access.

Filesystem `layout` placeholders are arrow-style tokens ({YYYY}, {MM}, {DD}, {load_id}, {file_id}, {ext}, {table_name}, {schema_name}, {curr_date}) — {year}/{month}/{day} raise InvalidFilesystemLayout. The exception text conveniently lists the full valid set.

Relative paths inside a DuckDB view's read_parquet() resolve against the DuckDB process's cwd at QUERY time, not at CREATE VIEW time. A view created from the pipeline directory will break when marimo opens the same warehouse.duckdb from elsewhere. Use absolute paths, or a DuckDB variable/macro for the lake root.

Two identical runs produce 240 rows for 120 distinct orders. Append-only is correct for DAS but das__staged as written duplicates rows — a dedup/latest-version step (QUALIFY ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY order_id ORDER BY das_extracted_at DESC)) is needed before DAB consumes it.

## Ingestion — /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-adss-2026-09-07/45a0041f-5559-570b-bd39-1d1517807233/scratchpad/spikes/spike1-dlt/recipe.py

    """DAS forgiving ingestion: one JSON column per source record, append-only parquet."""
    import os, uuid, hashlib, json
    from datetime import datetime, timezone
    import requests, dlt

    BASE = "https://demodata.grapecity.com/northwind/odata/v1/Orders"
    LAKE = os.path.abspath("./_lake3")
    PAGE = 60

    @dlt.resource(
        name="orders",
        write_disposition="append",
        columns={"payload": {"data_type": "json"}},   # <-- the whole trick
    )
    def odata_orders(page_size: int = PAGE, max_pages: int = 2):
        run_id = str(uuid.uuid4())
        for page in range(max_pages):
            url = f"{BASE}?$count=true&$top={page_size}&$skip={page * page_size}"
            resp = requests.get(url, timeout=60)
            resp.raise_for_status()
            fetched_at = datetime.now(timezone.utc)
            body = resp.json()
            for i, rec in enumerate(body["value"]):
                canon = json.dumps(rec, separators=(",", ":"), sort_keys=True)
                yield {
                    "payload":            rec,                      # stays ONE json column
                    "das_source_system":  "northwind_odata",
                    "das_source_entity":  "Orders",
                    "das_request_url":    url,
                    "das_http_status":    resp.status_code,
                    "das_extracted_at":   fetched_at,
                    "das_run_id":         run_id,
                    "das_page_number":    page,
                    "das_page_offset":    i,
                    "das_record_hash":    hashlib.sha256(canon.encode()).hexdigest(),
                    "das_source_count":   body.get("@odata.count"),
                }

    pipeline = dlt.pipeline(
        pipeline_name="das_ingest",
        destination=dlt.destinations.filesystem(
            bucket_url=LAKE,
            enable_dataset_name_normalization=False,   # keeps the literal 'das__raw'
            # optional: layout="{table_name}/load_date={YYYY}-{MM}-{DD}/{load_id}.{file_id}.{ext}",
        ),
        dataset_name="das__raw",
    )
    info = pipeline.run(odata_orders(), loader_file_format="parquet")

## Recommended provenance columns (dlt's two are NOT enough)

Keep `_dlt_load_id` + `_dlt_id`, and ADD, on every raw row:

| column | why |
|---|---|
| `das_source_system` | which upstream system ("northwind_odata") |
| `das_source_entity` | which endpoint/entity ("Orders") |
| `das_request_url`   | the exact URL incl. `$top`/`$skip` — answers "from where" per row |
| `das_http_status`   | proves the row came from a 200 |
| `das_extracted_at`  | wall-clock of the HTTP call — answers "when" WITHOUT joining `_dlt_loads` |
| `das_run_id`        | uuid4 per pipeline invocation — groups pages of one logical run |
| `das_page_number` / `das_page_offset` | position within the paginated fetch; makes a row reproducible |
| `das_record_hash`   | sha256 of canonical json — the ONLY stable record identity; use for dedup, since `_dlt_id` changes every load |
| `das_source_count`  | `@odata.count` at fetch time — lets you detect truncated pulls |

Do NOT rely on `_dlt_id` for identity and do NOT rely on `_dlt_load_id` alone for time — the timestamp lives in a separate JSONL file.

## DuckDB views — /tmp/claude-0/.../spike1-dlt/views.sql (use ABSOLUTE paths in production)

    CREATE SCHEMA IF NOT EXISTS das__raw;
    CREATE SCHEMA IF NOT EXISTS das__staged;

    -- LAYER 1: forgiving. one view per source entity over the append-only parquet glob.
    CREATE OR REPLACE VIEW das__raw.orders AS
    SELECT *, filename AS das_source_file
    FROM read_parquet(
           '_lake3/das__raw/orders/*.parquet',
           filename      => true,
           union_by_name => true   -- MANDATORY: without it DuckDB uses file #1's schema
                                   -- and silently drops columns added in later loads
         );

    -- LAYER 2: strict. explicit casts out of the JSON text column.
    CREATE OR REPLACE VIEW das__staged.orders AS
    SELECT
      CAST(payload ->> '$.OrderId'      AS BIGINT)         AS order_id,
            payload ->> '$.CustomerId'                     AS customer_id,
      CAST(payload ->> '$.EmployeeId'   AS INTEGER)        AS employee_id,
      TRY_CAST(payload ->> '$.OrderDate'   AS DATE)        AS order_date,
      TRY_CAST(payload ->> '$.ShippedDate' AS DATE)        AS shipped_date,
      CAST(payload ->> '$.Freight'      AS DECIMAL(18,4))  AS freight,
            payload ->> '$.ShipCountry'                    AS ship_country,
            payload ->> '$.ShipRegion'                     AS ship_region,
      json_keys(payload)                                   AS payload_keys,
      _dlt_load_id, _dlt_id,
      das_source_system, das_source_entity, das_request_url,
      das_extracted_at, das_run_id, das_page_number, das_page_offset,
      das_record_hash, das_source_count, das_source_file
    FROM das__raw.orders;

JSON functions DuckDB actually wants (all work on a plain VARCHAR column, implicit cast, no `::JSON` needed):
- `payload ->> '$.Field'`          -> VARCHAR (then wrap in CAST / TRY_CAST)
- `payload -> '$.a.b.c'`           -> JSON (nested navigation)
- `json_keys(payload)`             -> VARCHAR[]
- `json_array_length(payload,'$.Arr')` -> UINT64
- `json_extract(payload, '$.X')`   -> JSON

gotchas: dataset_name='das__raw' is SILENTLY renamed to 'das_raw' (dlt collapses the double underscore). Only a WARNING log line tells you. Fix: dlt.destinations.filesystem(bucket_url=..., enable_dataset_name_normalization=False). If DAS/DAB/DAR all use double-underscore schema names, every dlt destination in the project needs this flag.

DuckDB read_parquet over a glob defaults to the FIRST file's schema and silently drops columns present only in later files — no error, no warning, just missing data. In an append-only lake where you may add a provenance column, always pass union_by_name => true.

max_table_nesting=0 is NOT the answer to 'do not normalise'. It only stops child tables; top-level keys still become snake_cased typed columns. Only the payload+data_type='json' hint (or pre-serialising with json.dumps) gives one column.

dlt's `json` data_type is NOT a parquet JSON logical type. parquet_schema() shows BYTE_ARRAY / UTF8 / StringType() — byte-identical to a text column. Anything downstream reading the parquet sees a VARCHAR, so the strict layer must cast, always.

_dlt_id is regenerated per load. The same source record has a different _dlt_id in every run (10248 was b6aVmzfAxRVPDA then z8O+0F4oaJbS5A). Never use it as a business or record key — add your own content hash.

_dlt_loads, _dlt_pipeline_state and _dlt_version are written as .jsonl even when loader_file_format='parquet'. To get a load's completion timestamp you must read_json_auto() the JSONL, not read_parquet(). Better: put das_extracted_at on every row so das__staged never needs that join.

dlt inferred freight as DOUBLE when it normalised the record (approach C). Money silently becomes floating point. The strict layer casting to DECIMAL(18,4) out of the JSON string is the fix — another reason not to let dlt infer.

Schema evolution is real and late: ship_region only appeared as a column AFTER the first records that had it null, and it landed at the END of the column list. Column ORDER in the parquet is not stable across loads — never rely on positional access.

Filesystem `layout` placeholders are arrow-style tokens ({YYYY}, {MM}, {DD}, {load_id}, {file_id}, {ext}, {table_name}, {schema_name}, {curr_date}) — {year}/{month}/{day} raise InvalidFilesystemLayout. The exception text conveniently lists the full valid set.

Relative paths inside a DuckDB view's read_parquet() resolve against the DuckDB process's cwd at QUERY time, not at CREATE VIEW time. A view created from the pipeline directory will break when marimo opens the same warehouse.duckdb from elsewhere. Use absolute paths, or a DuckDB variable/macro for the lake root.

Two identical runs produce 240 rows for 120 distinct orders. Append-only is correct for DAS but das__staged as written duplicates rows — a dedup/latest-version step (QUALIFY ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY order_id ORDER BY das_extracted_at DESC)) is needed before DAB consumes it.

Whether enable_dataset_name_normalization=False also disables TABLE name normalisation was not tested — every table name I used was already snake_case. If a source entity is named 'OrderDetails' it may still normalise to 'order_details'; verify before relying on literal names.
